376564.title: The periodic even-size O(1) loop-model largest-component conjecture
376564.statement:

376599.title: Zero distribution conjecture for the second-largest spinless-fermion eigenvalue
376599.statement:
Let $p_0\in 2\mathbb{Z}$, and let $T^{(2)}_{n-1}(v)$ denote the corresponding fused transfer-matrix eigenvalue for the second-largest eigenvalue in the sector $N_{\rm e}=N/2-1$. The physical strip is $\operatorname{Im}v\in[-1,1]$.

**Zero distribution conjecture.** $T^{(2)}_{n-1}(v)$ has one real zero $\zeta_{n-1}$ for $n$ even with $2\leq n\leq p_0-1$, and two real zeros $\zeta_{n-1}$ and $-\zeta'_{n-1}$ for $n$ odd with $2<n<p_0/2$. All other zeros are outside the physical strip.

This conjecture describes the analyticity pattern needed to derive the nonlinear integral equations for the second-largest eigenvalue. It is based on numerical studies, and the supplied passage gives no resolution beyond that numerical evidence.

376613.title: Smallest $(r,r-1)$-erasure correcting set conjecture
376613.statement:
For each $r\geq 2$, let $A_{r,r-1}$ be the explicitly constructed $(r,r-1)$-erasure correcting set, and let $F(r,r-1)$ be the minimum cardinality of any such set. **Smallest-set conjecture.** If $r\geq 2$, then $A_{r,r-1}$ is a smallest possible $(r,r-1)$-erasure correcting set, and

$$
F(r,r-1)=2^{r-1}-1.
$$

This is presented as an unproved belief after the paper establishes related optimality results, including optimality of the construction for $m=r$.

376614.statement:

376621.title: MacWilliams identity conjecture for convolutional-code adjacency matrices
376621.statement:
Let ${\mathcal C}$ be a convolutional code over ${\mathbb F}$ with adjacency matrix $\Lambda$, and let $\widehat{\mathcal C}$ be its dual code with generalized adjacency matrix $\widehat\Lambda=(\widehat\lambda_{X,Y})$. Let $q=|{\mathbb F}|$, let $k$ be the dimension of ${\mathcal C}$, let $\delta$ be their common degree, let ${\mathcal H}$ be the MacWilliams matrix, and let $\text{${\text{\textbf H}}$}$ denote the corresponding entrywise transformation. For connected state pairs $(X,Y)\in{\mathcal F}$, there exists $P\in \operatorname{GL}_{\delta}({\mathbb F})$.

**MacWilliams identity conjecture.** The matrix

$$
q^{-k}\text{${\text{\textbf H}}$}\big({\mathcal H}\Lambda^t{\mathcal H}^{-1}\big)
$$

where $\text{${\text{\textbf H}}$}$ is applied entrywise, is a representative of the generalized adjacency matrix of $\widehat{\mathcal C}$; equivalently,

$$
\widehat\lambda_{X,Y}=q^{-k}\text{${\text{\textbf H}}$}\big(({{\mathcal H}\Lambda^t{\mathcal H}^{-1}})_{XP,YP}\big) \quad\text{for all }(X,Y)\in{\mathcal F}.
$$

This conjecture would extend the classical MacWilliams identity from block codes to convolutional codes by showing that the adjacency matrix of a code determines that of its dual through an explicit transformation. The surrounding section proves the identity for a particular class of codes, while the displayed assertion is formulated as the general conjectural statement.

376635.title: Brass's subpolygon Hausdorff-approximation conjecture
376635.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a family of convex polygons in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ that is closed under taking subpolygons, where a subpolygon is the convex hull of a subset of the polygon's vertices. Say that an element of $\mathcal{P}$ is hardest to approximate by its $k$-vertex subpolygons with respect to the Hausdorff metric if it has the worst such approximation error. **Brass's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{P}$ has an element that is hardest to approximate by its $k$-vertex subpolygons with respect to the Hausdorff metric, then one can also find a $(k+1)$-gon in $\mathcal{P}$ with this property. The paper proves the conjecture by showing that every worst-approximable polygon under Hausdorff approximation is a $(k+1)$-gon.

376648.title: The big-group deficiency conjecture
376648.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely presented group. Its **deficiency** is

$$
\operatorname{def}(\Gamma)=\max(g-r),
$$

where the maximum is taken over finite presentations of $\Gamma$ with $g$ generators and $r$ relations. A group is **big** in the sense used in the paper.

**Big-group deficiency conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ is a big group, then

$$
\operatorname{def}(\Gamma)\leq 0.
$$

The paper identifies this conjecture as equivalent to answering the zero-in-the-spectrum question affirmatively for universal covers of finite connected $2$-dimensional $CW$-complexes. Its resolution status is not given in the supplied text.

376697.title: The generating-function conjecture for multiple Clausen value irreducibles
376697.statement:
For weight $n$ and depth $k$, let $P(n,k)$ denote the number of irreducible multiple Clausen values such that a rational basis at that weight and depth is formed from a minimum number of irreducibles, augmented by products of irreducibles of lesser weight and depth. **Generating-function conjecture.** This weight-and-depth filtration is generated by

$$
\prod_{n>1,\,k>0}(1-x^ny^k)^{P(n,k)}=1-\frac{x^2y}{1-x}.
$$

This conjecture refines the preceding dimension-counting proposal by tracking both weight and depth. The paper gives it as a pattern suggested by computational experiments; no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.

376828.title: Aldous-Diaconis spectral-gap conjecture for the symmetric simple exclusion process
376828.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite graph, and let $L$ be the generator of the symmetric simple exclusion process with positive jump rates $J_{xy}$ on its edges. Let $H_\Lambda^{(n)}$ be the invariant subspace of configurations with exactly $n$ particles, and let $\lambda(n)$ denote the smallest positive eigenvalue of $L\vert_{H_\Lambda^{(n)}}$. **Aldous-Diaconis conjecture.**

$$
\lambda(n)=\lambda(1),\quad 1\leq n\leq\lvert\Lambda\rvert-1.
$$

Thus the spectral gap of the exclusion process is independent of the particle number, matching the one-particle spectral gap. The source attributes the conjecture to Aldous, while noting that Aldous said it arose in a conversation with Diaconis; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

377149.statement:
Let $X$ be a proper smooth scheme over $\mathbb C$. For integers $i,j$, define the coniveau filtration by

$$
N^iH^j(X)=\ker\left(H^j(X)\to\varinjlim_{\operatorname{codim}_X Z\geq i}H^j(X-Z)\right).
$$

The inclusion

$$
N^iH^j(X)_{\mathbb Q}\subseteq H^j(X,\mathbb Q)\cap F^iH^j(X)
$$

identifies the left-hand side with a subspace of rational Hodge classes. **Grothendieck–Hodge conjecture.** The space $N^iH^j(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the largest subspace of $H^j(X,\mathbb Q)\cap F^iH^j(X)$ whose complexification generates a sub-Hodge structure of $H^j(X,\mathbb C)$. This is a strengthening of the Hodge-coniveau comparison and is open in general.

377164.title: The Perron eigenvector conjecture for the O(1) loop-model Hamiltonian
377164.statement:

377246.title: The planar graph algebraic-connectivity conjecture
377246.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $a(G)$ denote its algebraic connectivity, the second-smallest eigenvalue of its Laplacian. $$

with equality if and only if $G=K_4$ or $G=2K_1\dot{+}C_4$. If $G$ is neither of these graphs, then $a(G)\leq 3$.

The conjecture would determine the maximum algebraic connectivity of planar graphs and its equality cases; the source reports that it has not been proved.

377430.title: The degree conjecture in nonpositive curvature
377430.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed $n$-manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature, negative Ricci curvature, and no local $\mathbb{R}$ factors. Let $N$ be any closed Riemannian manifold and let $f:N\longrightarrow M$ be any continuous map. **Degree conjecture in nonpositive curvature.** There is a constant $C>0$, depending only on $n$ and the smallest Ricci curvatures of $N$ and $M$, such that

$$
\operatorname{deg}(f)\leq C\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(N)}{\operatorname{Vol}(M)}.
$$

The conjecture is known for negatively curved targets and, up to the stated exceptions, for locally symmetric targets by the degree theorem; the general nonpositively curved case remains open.

377505.title: Lipeomorphic invariance of metric-coordinate dimension
377505.statement:
Let $(M,d)$ and $(N,e)$ be metric spaces. A **lipeomorphism** between them is a bijective Lipschitz map whose inverse is also Lipschitz. The metric-coordinate dimension of a metric space is the smallest cardinal number $I$ such that every point has a neighborhood metrically coordinatized by a set of cardinality $I$.

**Lipeomorphic invariance conjecture.** Metric-coordinate dimension is invariant under lipeomorphisms; that is, if $M$ and $N$ are lipeomorphic, then they have the same metric-coordinate dimension.

This would show that metric-coordinate dimension, although not a homeomorphic invariant, is preserved by the stronger equivalence relation of lipeomorphism. The source states the claim without providing evidence of a proof or disproof.

377717.title: The rank conjecture for free actions on products of spheres
377717.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $G$ act freely on

$$
X=\mathbb S^{n_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb S^{n_m}.

$$
r(G)\le m.
$$

377763.title: Interpolation conjecture for the calculus of structures
377763.statement:
Let $T$ and $R$ be structures, and let $\mathsf{SKS}$ denote the calculus-of-structures system for classical propositional logic. Write $\mathsf{SKS}\setminus\{\mathord{\downarrow}\text{-identity},\mathord{\downarrow}\text{-weakening}\}$ and $\mathsf{SKS}\setminus\{\mathord{\uparrow}\text{-identity},\mathord{\uparrow}\text{-weakening}\}$ for the systems obtained by omitting the indicated rules.

**Interpolation conjecture.** For every derivation $T\vdash_{\mathsf{SKS}}R$, there is a structure $P$ and derivations

$$
T\vdash_{\mathsf{SKS}\setminus\{\text{identity},\text{weakening}\}}P
$$

and

$$
P\vdash_{\mathsf{SKS}\setminus\{\text{dual identity},\text{dual weakening}\}}R.
$$

The derivation is separated into a top phase whose rules do not introduce new atoms going down and a bottom phase whose rules do not introduce new atoms going up; consequently, $P$ contains only atoms occurring in both $T$ and $R$ and is an interpolant. The source states that a semantic proof is available in the propositional case, while a syntactic proof extending to predicate logic remains desirable.

377818.title: The partition polynomial convolution identity
377818.statement:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d)$ be a finite sequence with sum

$$
s(\Lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i.
$$

Define the polynomial $F_\Lambda(x)$ by $F_\emptyset(x)=1$ and, for $1\leq d=\sharp(\Lambda)<\infty$,

$$
F_\Lambda(x)=x{x-1+s(\Lambda)\choose d-1}(d-1)!.
$$

For a map $\varphi\colon\{1,\dots,d\}\to\{1,\dots,k\}$, let $\varphi^{-1}(1),\dots,\varphi^{-1}(k)$ be the induced sub-sequences of $\Lambda$. **Partition polynomial convolution identity.** For arbitrary $x_1,\dots,x_k$, one has

$$
\sum_{\varphi\in\{1,\dots,k\}^{\{1,\dots,d\}}}\prod_{j=1}^k F_{\varphi^{-1}(j)}(x_j)=F_\Lambda\left(\sum_{j=1}^k x_j\right).
$$

This is presented as an identity rather than an explicitly named conjecture; the supplied parser nevertheless identifies it as a conjecture environment, and no proof or resolution information is provided in the source excerpt.

377920.title: Mestre bound sharpness conjecture over number fields
377920.statement:
Fix a number field $F$. For each positive integer $N$, let $r_F(N)$ be the maximum of $\operatorname{Rank}_{\mathbb{Z}}E(F)$ over elliptic curves $E/F$ whose conductor $\mathfrak{n}_E$ has norm $N$, and set $r_F(N)=0$ if no such curve exists. **Mestre bound sharpness conjecture.** One has

$$
